keyVerseText: For I say unto you, That except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven.
rootMeaning: The Greek adjective πλείων (pleíōn) is the comparative form of πολύς (polýs), meaning 'much' or 'many.' As a comparative, πλείων literally conveys the idea of 'more' in quantity, size, or extent, emphasizing an increase or superiority relative to something else. This root sense enriches the English glosses by highlighting not just abundance but a surpassing or exceeding quality, suggesting something greater or more excellent rather than merely numerous.
usageInScripture: Throughout Scripture, πλείων appears 56 times and is most frequently translated as 'more' (14 occurrences) and 'many' (8 occurrences), with other renderings like 'more than,' 'a greater than,' and 'most' reflecting its comparative nature. It is used to denote superiority in number, quality, or degree, whether referring to time, quantity, or extent. This range of usage underscores its consistent role in expressing something that surpasses a standard or majority, often in both literal and figurative senses.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding πλείων as a term denoting surpassing or exceeding is vital for grasping biblical concepts of righteousness, abundance, and the kingdom of God. It challenges believers to pursue a faith and life that go beyond mere adequacy or external conformity, aiming instead for a deeper, more excellent righteousness. This aligns with the biblical call to live by the Spirit and not merely by the letter of the law, emphasizing growth in grace and truth. The word's comparative force invites Christians to reflect on the surpassing worth of Christ's righteousness and the greater life He offers.
keyVerseReflection: In Matthew 5:20, Jesus declares that one's righteousness must 'exceed' (πλείων) that of the scribes and Pharisees to enter the kingdom of heaven. The use of πλείων here highlights not just more righteousness in quantity but a superior kind of righteousness—one that surpasses external legalism and embodies true heart transformation. This word powerfully communicates the necessity of a deeper, more excellent righteousness that only Christ can produce in believers, setting the standard for authentic discipleship.
